To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a fiber-optic localized surface plasmon resonance (FO LSP) sensor was fabricated and applied as a label-free immuno-assay for the detection of interferon-gamm (IFN-ɣ) and prostate-specific antigen ( PSA).

a Fiber-Optical Localized Surface Plasmom Resonance (LSPR) biosensor was fabricated using spherical Au nanoparticles (NPs) on a flat end face of the optical fiber, and was applied for label free immunoassay.
the proposed FO LSPR biosensor is able to measure IFN-gamma and PSA in the concentration of 2 and 1pg/ml with a high resolution and sensitivity, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new label-free optical biosensor for the detection of biomarkers in the fields of medical diagnostics and environmental analysis.
the fabrication of a FO LSPR-based sensor for label-free immoassay of IFN-γ and PSA.
the development of a simple, fast, and sensitive label-free immuno-sensing platform using the FO LSPRs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed FO LSPR biosensor can be a useful platform for real-time label free immunoassay and can be used for the development of a point-of-care diagnostic system.
a FO LSPR biosensor was developed and used for real-time detection of IFN-γ and PSA with LOD of 2pg/ml and 1pg/ml, respectively.
this work demonstrates a simple, low-cost, and real-time detection method of the label-free immuno-assay using the FO LSPRsensor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully demonstrated the possibility of using the FO LSPRsensor as a biosensor in label-free immuno-assay for the detection of IFN-γ and PSA.
this study is a significant step forward in the field of label-free immuno-sensing.
we fabricated a FO LSPR based immunoassay system using spherical Au NPs and demonstrated the detection of two different biomolecules, IFN-γ and PSA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed FO LSPR biosensors are promising for the detection of biomarkers in the early diagnosis of cancer and infectious diseases, and for in-vivo detection.
the FO LSPRsensor can be used for label-free immuoassays of biomolecules and the LOD of the proposed FO LSPR biosensor is comparable to the LOD of the SPR biosensor.
